title: PowerPoint on desktop: Copilot Agent Mode creates executive summary slides
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and licence-assignment instructions match the sources checked. It appropriately distinguishes general Copilot licensing and rollout guidance from the unpublished details of executive summary slides.

claims.claim: Microsoft names no administrator action for this feature in the evidence checked.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode executive summary slides licensing default admin settings prerequisites data access; read roadmap 555876, Copilot settings and release notes. No feature-specific administrator action was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe this specific executive-summary-slide feature at the time of writing.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) uses organisational data through Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.
claims.quote: **Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)** uses **both** web and organizational data via [Microsoft Graph](/en-us/graph/overview) and [Work IQ](/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/), and pulls information automatically.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic), Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) have Enterprise Data Protection with Microsoft Entra sign-in.

claims.claim: Learn describes no identity or permission model specific to executive summary slides.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "summary" "Agent Mode" default permissions identity admin switch; PowerPoint Agent Mode executive summary slides licensing default admin settings prerequisites data access. Read overview, settings and release-note matches; no slide-specific identity model.

claims.claim: No change to who can see the deck or its slides is documented for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "summary" "Agent Mode" default permissions identity admin switch. Read overview and settings; searched release notes for executive and summary slide. No executive-summary-slide visibility change was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users lack the Copilot add-on but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You **don't** have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but **can** use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the add-on licensed experience with full Copilot access in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You **have** the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic) alone does not give access to Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You **don't** have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and **don't** have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Scope: Users; Governance controls; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint has Basic and Premium licence experiences, represented as mixed licensing.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic): You **don't** have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but **can** use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium): You **have** the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses is the licence-assignment route.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the **Users** > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select **Licenses and Apps**. Expand the **Licenses** section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a user licence through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least a License or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The Graph PowerShell licence-assignment route requires User.ReadWrite.All or another permission listed in the Assign license Graph API reference.
claims.quote: Assigning and removing licenses for a user requires the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope or one of the other permissions listed in the ['Assign license' Microsoft Graph API reference page](/en-us/graph/api/user-assignlicense).
